title: Batching heuristics lab notes
content:
Context: quick personal lab scratchpad to track microbatching experiments and heuristics for small-model VCPU fallback and KV prefetch interplay. Goal is to reduce p99 for short requests (<32 tokens) while keeping token cost acceptable.

Notes and recent observations:
- Observation (2026-03-09 prod window): p99 spike correlated with small bursts of ~30 concurrent short requests. Throughput steady but tail increases ~30-45ms. No obvious CPU saturation on serving nodes.
- Hypothesis A: continuous batching introduces serialization delay for low-latency short requests when batch windows enlarge under certain traffic shapes.
- Hypothesis B: KV prefetching (when enabled) occasionally blocks steam processing path for first-token retrieval due to lock contention on local KV cache for hot prefixes.
- Observation: enabling kv_prefetch=true reduced cold-start latency on long sequences but seemed to add 10-20ms variance for 4-16 token requests in synthetic replay.

Quick experiments run locally (devbox-g4dn):
1) baseline: batch_window_ms=6, max_batch_tokens=2048, kv_prefetch=false
   - replay (rps=150, load shape: poisson bursts): p50=12ms, p95=28ms, p99=54ms
2) batch_window_ms=3, kv_prefetch=false
   - p50=10ms, p95=22ms, p99=42ms (improvement on tail but throughput drop 5%)
3) batch_window_ms=3, kv_prefetch=true, kv_lock_timeout=2ms
   - p50=11ms, p95=26ms, p99=48ms (prefetch helps median for long sequences but tail slightly worse vs no prefetch)
4) dynamic-window (adaptive by concurrency): if concurrency<20 => window=2ms else window=6ms, kv_prefetch=true
   - p50=10ms, p95=23ms, p99=39ms (best tail so far in dev)

Command snippets I used:
- run replay: ./tools/replay_client --config experiments/short-burst.json --concurrency 150 --rps 150
- start local node: ./bin/serve --dev-mode --profile small-vcpu --port 8081
- capture flame: ./bin/trace-capture --pid $(pgrep serve) --out /tmp/trace-fold.json

Trace takeaways:
- majority of tail time is spent in: batching_coordinator.wait_for_batch + kv_cache.lookup (contended) + response_serialization
- critical path shows blocking syscall in epoll_wait when burst arrives; could be due to worker threads parked because batch coordinator sleeps until window expiry.

Open hypotheses to validate (ordered):
- H1: make batch window adaptive to per-route request size distribution (short-route special-casing). Test: route-level config override with window=1-2ms for low-token routes.
- H2: introduce optimistic KV lookup without locks: try lock-free read path for cache hits and fall back to locked write for misses. Prototype in runtime/cache/fast_read branch.
- H3: offload response serialization to dedicated worker pool to reduce blocking in token generation worker.

Proposed quick roadmap (for next 5 working days):
- Day 1: add route-level batch_window override, run 48h replay vs prod trace. (Owner: me)
- Day 2: prototype lock-free KV read path (Owner: Rajiv). Add metrics: kv_lock_wait_ms histogram.
- Day 3: small experiment: dedicate 2 serialization threads and measure p99 with current load (Owner: Maya).
- Day 4: combine best knobs (adaptive window + lock-free reads + serialization pool) in staging, run chaos test with spiky arrival patterns.
- Day 5: write a short runbook snippet for ops: when p99>50ms for short route, try toggling route.window -> 2ms then disable kv_prefetch.

Quick TODOs (my personal):
- [ ] push route-level window patch to feature branch (branch: batch-route-window/amf)
- [ ] add unit tests for new config parsing (YAML) for route overrides
- [ ] add kv_lock_wait_ms metric and wire into console dashboard (console-metrics ticket created)
- [ ] create small benchmark harness to replay real prod traces with preserved inter-arrival timestamps
- [ ] sync with Maya about serialization worker pool safety (race conditions?)

Open questions to ask on next pairing with Rajiv:
- Does the current KV cache implementation have any read-side atomicity guarantees that block lock-free reads? Where do we risk ABA issues?
- What are CPU implications of reducing batch_window to 1-2ms at 200 rps sustained? Estimate: 8-12% extra CPU cycles due to smaller batches. Need SRE signoff for Dedicated customers.

Reference notes / links I keep hitting:
- ticket RINF-5822: "p99 spikes for short-token routes during bursts" (linked)
- PR draft: runtime#1589 notes about batching refactor and coordinator backoff behavior
- perf dashboard: /console/dashboards/serving/runtime-batching (watch p99, cpu util, batch size)

Misc scratch bits:
- micro idea: pre-seed batch buffer with high-priority short requests to avoid long waits for first token (complex: fairness tradeoff)
- smaller model fallback: if detected short request distribution and spare vcpu, route to small-quantized variant with lower cost but faster first-token speed
- note to self: remember to add a flag so ops can force-disable kv_prefetch per route without a full redeploy

End of pad. Will update after Day 1 run.

Small sign-off: leaving a few loose timings I recorded locally:
- 2026-03-10 21:03:12 replay run: mean batch size ~6, cpu% avg 38, p99 41ms
- 2026-03-11 09:14:58 staging: adaptive-window test: mean batch size ~4, p99 37ms
